title: Pittsburgh Paint Company Booms as Big Tech Builds AI Data
summary: A 143-year-old Pittsburgh paint firm sees record growth supplying coatings for Microsoft, Google, and Amazon AI data center construction projects.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- A Pittsburgh paint manufacturer founded in 1883 reports record sales supplying protective coatings for AI data center construction.
- Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are driving demand with massive infrastructure projects to support generative AI workloads.
- The boom highlights how AI's physical infrastructure needs are creating unexpected winners across traditional industrial sectors.


A 143-year-old Pittsburgh paint manufacturer is experiencing its most profitable period ever, driven by an unprecedented surge in AI data center construction. The company, which has supplied industrial coatings since 1883, now finds itself at the center of Big Tech's race to build the physical infrastructure powering generative AI models. Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have become the firm's largest customers as they rapidly expand data center capacity to support compute-intensive AI workloads.


## Record Growth From AI Infrastructure Demand


The paint company reported a 340% year-over-year revenue increase in Q3 2026, with AI-related data center projects accounting for 78% of total sales. The firm specializes in high-performance protective coatings designed for industrial facilities, including fire-resistant paints, thermal barrier systems, and electromagnetic shielding materials critical to data center operations. Orders have doubled every quarter since early 2026 as hyperscale cloud providers accelerate construction timelines to meet AI computing demands.


Officially launched on November 3, 2026, the company's expanded production facility in Pittsburgh will triple manufacturing capacity by Q2 2027. The $47 million investment includes new mixing lines, quality control labs, and logistics infrastructure to handle the volume of orders from tech companies building hundreds of new data centers across North America.


## Big Tech's Data Center Construction Sprint


Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are collectively investing over $180 billion in data center infrastructure through 2027, according to industry analysts. The buildout supports training runs for next-generation large language models and inference workloads for deployed AI applications. Each hyperscale data center requires specialized coatings for server rooms, cooling systems, electrical infrastructure, and exterior surfaces, creating sustained demand for industrial paint suppliers.


- Microsoft plans 35 new AI-optimized data centers by end of 2027
- Google is expanding existing campuses and building 22 greenfield sites
- Amazon Web Services targeting 50+ facilities to support Bedrock AI services


The paint company's CEO noted in a statement that lead times for orders have extended from six weeks to four months, with some customers placing advance orders for 2027 delivery to secure supply. The firm has hired 230 additional employees this year and is recruiting chemists and production specialists to meet ongoing demand.


## Specialized Coatings For AI Infrastructure


AI data centers require more demanding environmental controls than traditional facilities. Training clusters for frontier models like GPT-6 and Gemini 4 generate intense heat loads, requiring advanced thermal management systems. The Pittsburgh firm's portfolio includes intumescent coatings that expand under heat to protect structural elements, along with conductive paints that help dissipate electromagnetic interference from dense GPU arrays.


Water-based coatings with low volatile organic compound content have become particularly valuable as data center operators face stricter environmental regulations. The company's research division is developing new formulations optimized for liquid cooling systems, which are becoming standard in next-generation AI compute infrastructure.


## What This Means


The Pittsburgh paint company's trajectory illustrates how AI's infrastructure requirements are creating opportunities far beyond the technology sector itself. As frontier AI models demand exponentially more compute resources, the physical buildout of data centers is generating demand across construction materials, industrial equipment, power systems, and specialized manufacturing. Legacy companies with deep technical expertise in industrial applications are finding themselves essential partners in the AI era, proving that the technology's impact extends well beyond software and semiconductors into the traditional industrial economy.
